clue.text: Merci, la Mafia!

parts.note: the French word for thanks is what you get when the letters of a word for wrongdoing are put in order, i.e. rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A grateful French exclamation addressed to the Mafia.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'organised' as an anagram signal applied to a five-letter word for wrongdoing, and you get MERCI. 'la Mafia' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is the classic example of a syndicate running racketeering and other systematic lawbreaking.

clue.text: Not a good time to reap — some room for improvement

indicators.note: the letters are to be improved upon, worked into a better arrangement

explanation.surface: Harvest time is bad: there is scope to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: Cicero's Latin cry 'O the times, O the customs!' laments a bad age, hence 'Not a good time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin exclamation laments the corrupt manners of the present era.

clue.text: Philistine's end in piggyback

indicators.note: back, the tail of piggyback, says the whole piece is read in reverse
in puts the end piece inside the pig piece

parts.note: a piggy is a pig, which is also a hog
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: The setter, Philistine, signs off in a piggyback ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle signs as Philistine, so the definition is self-referential. 'piggyback' must be split: 'piggy' gives the outer piece and 'back' turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant slain by David in the Bible was a champion of the Philistines.

clue.text: Fiery stuff served up with baked beans garnish in Portsmouth?

indicators.note: the volcanic piece garnishes the bean letters by being set among them
baked beans are cooked, so their letters are reworked
in a down clue served up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lava is the molten rock from a volcano

explanation.surface: A hot sauce dished up with a topping on baked beans in a naval town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' signals an anagram of the beans, and 'served up' turns the fiery stuff upwards in this down clue. Portsmouth is a south-coast English city, home of the Royal Navy; the question mark shows it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Portsmouth is the historic home port of the British fleet, an example of a navy harbour station.

clue.text: Passages transgress on forms of employment

parts.note: to sin is to transgress
uses are ways of employing something

explanation.surface: Passages in a text breach various employment rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuses are hollow cavities and channels in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Talk about an athletic event with squad leader

parts.note: the discus is a field event in athletics

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of squad

explanation.surface: Debate over a field event with the team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a topic is to talk it over with others.

clue.text: In some way, the poor are rich (but that's relatively unusual)

indicators.note: in some way says the answer is lodged in part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A paradox: the poor are rich in a sense, though that is uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer is less common, unusual by comparison.

clue.text: Host welcomes military clique's demoted leader, a beast

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, putting the clique piece inside the host piece

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a host

indicators.note: demoted leader means the first letter is moved further down the word

parts.note: a junta is a military clique ruling a country

explanation.surface: A host receives the ousted head of an army regime, a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demoted leader' means the clique's first letter slides down within the word rather than being dropped; the result then sits inside the host's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The muntjac is a small Asian deer, now common wild in England.

clue.text: Coldplay's latest hit (newer compilation)

definitions.note: a cryptic way of saying a play whose title is about the cold season

indicators.note: a compilation puts material together in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new hits album containing the band Coldplay's latest single.
explanation.walkthrough: Coldplay looks like the British band, but split it: cold play, a drama named after the coldest season.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance has a frosty season in its title, making it a play about the cold.

clue.text: Invigorate and put the heart back in metropolitan evil neighbourhood

indicators.note: back says the letters taken from the phrase are read backwards
the heart of the three-word phrase is its middle, where the wanted letters sit across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A call to revive a wicked inner-city district.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Invigorate and put the heart' as the definition, but only 'Invigorate' defines; 'put the heart back' is the instruction. Read NEVILNE, from the middle of the phrase, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate something is to liven it up and give it fresh energy.

clue.text: A hundred compete in school squash

indicators.note: in places the hundred and the compete pieces within the school abbreviation

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to run in a race or election is to compete

explanation.surface: Someone enters a hundred-strong race at a school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash something is to crush or crumple it, as in crushing paper in a fist.

clue.text: It's a gem of a conference, perhaps with fifty in attendance

parts.note: Conference is a well-known variety of pear grown in Britain, so it is an example of the fruit
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Praise for a conference that was excellent and well attended by fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conference' looks like a meeting, but it is the British pear variety; 'perhaps' shows it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a lustrous gem formed inside an oyster, prized in jewellery.

clue.text: Perhaps T-bone makes one look masculine

definitions.note: the definition describes a noun phrase by what it does: a feature that makes one look masculine

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so a T is perhaps a square
the jaw is a bone of the face

explanation.surface: Eating a T-bone steak supposedly makes a person look more manly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T-bone' suggests a steak; split it as T (a T-square being a square) plus bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad, angular lower face is traditionally seen as a rugged, manly facial feature.

clue.text: Runs through the centre of Florence with several black cars in pursuit

indicators.note: in pursuit means following behind, so the black cars come after the letters from the city
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the middle pair of an eight-letter name

parts.note: hearses are the black cars that carry coffins at funerals

explanation.surface: A funeral cortege drives through the middle of the Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play or speech is to practise it, going over it from start to finish.

clue.text: Tinned American

definitions.meaning: split as ..., preserved in a tin
the Inca people were native South Americans, so this adjective names something from the Americas

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it means preserved in a can; whole it describes the Inca civilisation of the Andes.

clue.text: Compiler's on time and solver reported unprepared

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, writing as I, and compiler's is I'm, I am
prompt means punctual, on time

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the word is said rather than written

parts.note: the solver is you, addressed by the setter

explanation.surface: The setter says the puzzle is on time, and the solver is said to be unready.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, without rehearsal.

clue.text: Even board members, having dined, give a speech

indicators.note: even here means the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, of the word board

parts.note: having dined means having eaten, ate

explanation.surface: Even the directors have to make an after-dinner speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' says the letters of 'board' are the members chosen from; 'Even' picks O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal public address, often pompously.

clue.text: A radio personality in a hairstyle that's a mess

indicators.note: in places the radio piece inside the hairstyle

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
a DJ, disc jockey, is a radio personality

explanation.surface: A radio presenter with an untidy haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad job is a botched piece of work, a shambles.

clue.text: Incompetent at home, father gets entangled in flex

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: gets entangled in puts the father piece inside the flex piece

parts.note: flex is the British word for an electric cable
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A clumsy dad at home trips over the electric lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incapable lacks the ability to do a task, so is unfit or useless at it.

clue.text: Supporting dissolute Floridian without taking sides

indicators.note: dissolute suggests something loose, so the letters are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: left and right are the two sides, abbreviated L and R

explanation.surface: A debauched man from Florida refuses to take part in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without taking' removes L and R (the sides) from FLORIDIAN; the remaining FOIDIAN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done to help a cause is for its benefit, backing it.

clue.text: Boxes boxes sweetheart makes

indicators.note: the second boxes is a verb, putting one piece around another

parts.note: crates are boxes
the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone boxes up what a lover makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To create something is to make or produce it.

clue.text: Custom-made bike frame and wheel component

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outside letters, the first and last

parts.note: a spoke is a rod from hub to rim of a wheel

explanation.surface: A bicycle with a tailored frame and a wheel part.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke goods, especially suits, are tailored to the individual buyer.

clue.text: Typically working, say, a long time

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
to aver is to say or assert
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Usually someone works, say, for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true in general or as a rule is true taking the mean of all cases.

clue.text: State of mutant genotype after one gets up and leaves

indicators.note: a mutant has altered genes, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A gene variant changes after one part rises and departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up and leaves' takes ONE out of GENOTYPE; the remaining GTYPE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country in North Africa, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Haven of Love by Status Quo

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
the status quo is things as they are, as is

explanation.surface: A song title credited to the rock band Status Quo.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo is a British rock band, and Oasis another, which makes the surface a music reference; here it means 'as is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, figuratively any peaceful refuge.

clue.text: French Beaujolais, in essence: lovely fine red finally appreciated

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its middle two letters here
finally picks the closing letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A wine lover's tasting note praising a fine French red.
explanation.definitionFit: To have enjoyed something is to have taken pleasure in it and valued it.

clue.text: Take pies or cake — all 50% starch

indicators.note: all 50% asks for the first half of every one of the four words

explanation.surface: An offer of pies or cake at a sale with everything half price.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy food extracted from cassava root, used in puddings.

clue.text: Part of a lover that's rather tight

parts.note: a bit of something is a part of it
squeeze is informal slang for a boyfriend or girlfriend

explanation.surface: A romantic partner's embrace that is a little too snug.
explanation.definitionFit: When space is cramped, fitting in is described as a tight fit, scarcely enough room.
